appraisal_events.evidence: «il lui arrivait de détacher une fleur de son corsage, un médaillon et de les donner à quelqu'un» ... «Leur affection ne survit pas à l'exaltation qui la dicte» ... «le ur permettra ... de saisir vos ridicules et d'en amuser un autre de leurs visiteurs»
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator praises Mme de Guermantes' spontaneous verbal grace and generosity in the moment, but then ironically undercuts it as fleeting and insincere, noting the same wit will later mock the very person it flattered.

appraisal_events.evidence: «Oh ! quelle bonne idée ... voilà un homme intelligent» ... «l'ironie des valets se changeait en respect et que les invités s'empressaient autour de moi»
appraisal_events.explanation: After feeling shame under the guests' disdainful smiles for wearing snow-boots, the narrator is publicly praised by the princess, which visibly reverses the servants' mockery into respect and draws the guests' eager attention to him.

status_effects.explanation: Her effusive charm is narratively reframed as fickle and self-serving, producing a mild negative reassessment despite the surface praise of her grace.
The narrator moves from an object of quiet ridicule among the household staff and guests to one of admiration and curiosity, a modest but real local elevation.

ambiguities: The reflection on effusive but ultimately insincere affection blends a specific description of Mme de Guermantes' behavior with a generalized portrait of 'ces femmes' as a social type, so the diminishment may target the type as much as the individual.
